name: Kelly Ortberg

career.title: Program manager, rising through leadership roles (incl. VP and GM, Communication Systems, from 2001)
Special advisor to the CEO office; board member

background_rationale: A mechanical engineer who started at Texas Instruments and rose from program manager to CEO at avionics maker Rockwell Collins before leading Boeing.

notable.summary: Chose to base himself in the Seattle area near Boeing's main commercial aircraft plants, more than two decades after the company moved its headquarters out of Seattle.
Announced plans to cut about 17,000 jobs, roughly 10% of Boeing's global workforce, and delayed first 777X deliveries by a year, as Boeing also launched a large share sale to shore up cash.
Boeing ended a nearly two-month machinists' strike after workers accepted a contract with a 38% pay rise over four years and a $12,000 ratification bonus.
Agreed to sell Jeppesen and other parts of Boeing's Digital Aviation Solutions business to private equity firm Thoma Bravo for $10.55 billion.

personal_story.hook: A Dubuque-born mechanical engineer, Kelly Ortberg left retirement in 2024 to run Boeing.
personal_story.summary: Ortberg was born in 1960 and is a native of Dubuque, Iowa. He earned a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Iowa in 1982 and started his career as an engineer at Texas Instruments in 1983. In 1987 he joined Cedar Rapids-based Rockwell Collins as a program manager and spent more than three decades there, becoming CEO in 2013 and leading Collins Aerospace after its sale to United Technologies. He retired from RTX in 2021, then returned in August 2024 as Boeing's CEO, saying 'there is much work to be done.'
